members.name: _shouldRenderItems
members.description:
lazy-children: a nested list renders once its submenu has opened, or
when the selected item is somewhere inside it (so the active trail is
always in the DOM and can open itself). Once rendered it stays rendered.

members.name: hasVisibleChildren
members.description:
Whether an item has at least one direct child that is not hidden from
the menu. When this is false the builder renders the item as a leaf
(map-menu-item) instead of a collapsible submenu, so we never show an
expand arrow that opens to nothing. Recursion handles deeper levels:
a child that itself has no visible children also renders as a leaf, so
empty collapses are pruned at every depth.

declarations.name: MAP_MENU_PROGRESS_STATES
declarations.description:
Active page ring (haxtheweb/issues#3267): the item of the page open now
(activeProgress, 0 to 1, set by site-menu) shows a DDD progress ring
around its icon area, filled to that page's percent and turning into a
filled disc with a check once the page is done; the first time it
completes while open the ring bursts once (DDDBlock.js). Its percent is
the link's hover text and is spoken after the title. Other items show no
ring. Colours: --map-menu-progress-ring-color, --map-menu-progress-ring-
track, --map-menu-progress-ring-on-color (defaults read on a dark active
row in light mode and a light one in dark mode).

Learner progress marks for menu items (the progress property; site-menu
no longer sets it, it is kept so menus that do still work). `progress` is one of
"done", "in-progress", "visited" or "not-started"; anything else draws
nothing, so menus without progress data look exactly as before. Each mark
is a ring with a glyph (check, half, dot, empty) plus spoken text after the
title, so state never relies on colour alone.

declarations.name: MapMenuProgressStrings
declarations.default: { progressDone: "Done", progressInProgress: "In progress", progressVisited: "Visited", progressPercentComplete: "{percent}% complete", progressComplete: "Complete", }

declarations.name: mapMenuActiveRingStyles
declarations.default: [ DDDProgressRingStyles, css` /* the ring is drawn in the active row's own text colour (and the check on the done disc in the row's background), so every part of it has the contrast the theme gives its active text, at least 3:1 in any palette, light or dark. Progress reads as a thick arc over a thin full track, never colour alone. */ .active-ring { display: inline-flex; flex: none; align-self: center; /* the ring is taller than a line of the menu; keep the row height */ margin: calc(-1 * var(--ddd-spacing-2)) var(--ddd-spacing-2) calc(-1 * var(--ddd-spacing-2)) 0; --ddd-component-progress-ring-color: var( --map-menu-progress-ring-color, var( --map-menu-item-a-active-color, var(--map-menu-item-a-color, currentColor) ) ); --ddd-component-progress-ring-track: var( --map-menu-progress-ring-track, var( --map-menu-item-a-active-color, var(--map-menu-item-a-color, currentColor) ) ); --ddd-component-progress-ring-on-color: var( --map-menu-progress-ring-on-color, var(--map-menu-item-a-active-background-color, black) ); --ddd-component-progress-ring-size: var( --map-menu-progress-ring-size, var(--ddd-icon-xs) ); --ddd-component-progress-ring-width: 3.5; --ddd-component-progress-ring-track-width: 1.25; --ddd-component-progress-ring-empty-opacity: 1; } /* an item with children: the ring traces its expand control (the a11y-collapse chevron, 24px at 4px from the start of the row), so there is one control, not a ring beside a chevron */ .active-ring.on-expand { position: absolute; top: 50%; left: var(--map-menu-progress-ring-expand-left, 2px); margin: 0; transform: translateY(-50%); pointer-events: none; /* the chevron is 24px: a 28px ring traces it without reaching the title that starts right after it */ --ddd-component-progress-ring-size: var( --map-menu-progress-ring-expand-size, 28px ); } .active-ring.on-expand .ddd-ring-glyph { display: none; } `, ]

declarations.name: buildMenuTree

parameters.name: data
parameters.description: flat item list (each item: id, parent, ...)

declarations.description:
Turn a flat JSON Outline Schema item list into the nested tree map-menu
renders, in one pass over the data.

Same result as map-menu's original _dataChanged/_setChildren (which ran a
full filter of the list for every item): the top level is every item
without a parent, in data order; each item reached from the top gets a
`children` array of the items whose parent is its id, in data order. Like
the original, it sets `children` on the item objects themselves and leaves
items that can't be reached from the top level untouched.
